title: Validator‑Guided Repair on a Shared Initial LLM Candidate: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation for Network Configuration Safety
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01) to measure whether a generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline changes the executability of LLM‑produced network configurations when the same single sampled candidate per intent is deterministically reused across baseline and guarded arms (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Using gpt‑5‑mini (declared) to produce one initial generation per intent and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) with one permitted automated repair in the guarded arm, we ran the preregistered paired design on N = 200 intents (planned_episode_count = 400). Execution used 200 model calls (one shared initial generation per pair). Results: baseline_success_count = 200/200 and guarded_success_count = 200/200 (100% each); contingency: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0]. No repairs were applied because every shared initial candidate was validator‑valid (repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0). We report preregistration and execution accounting, representative validator traces, and an artifact‑grounded interpretation: under shared_initial_candidate semantics the experiment measures only downstream validator/repair effects on an identical sampled candidate; the observed degenerate null effect does not imply GVR methods are ineffective under independent sampling. We close with artifact‑grounded recommendations for follow‑on preregistered designs that change the estimand to test repair efficacy under realistic sampling variability.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) are being investigated for intent→configuration workflows in network operations (NetOps). Incorrect or unsafe device configurations produced by LLMs (hallucinations, syntactic mistakes, ordering errors) pose operational risk when applied to routers, switches, or other infrastructure. Generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipelines—LLM generation followed by deterministic verification and optional automated repair—are a plausible mitigation architecture. However, the empirical effect of GVR depends critically on experimental sampling semantics: whether each experimental arm receives independent first‑pass samples or both arms reuse the same generated candidate. We preregistered and executed a narrowly scoped confirmatory paired study to measure the downstream effect of validation and a single allowed automated repair on the same LLM candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Research question: Does applying deterministic validation plus one automated repair to a fixed single LLM candidate per intent change the rate of validator‑valid, executable configurations relative to reusing that same candidate without validation/repair? Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01) with deterministic artifact capture and reproducible analysis; (2) an artifact‑grounded execution on 200 paired intents using gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with exact per‑condition accounting and provider audit evidence; (3) a transparent interpretation of a degenerate null paired effect arising from shared_initial_candidate semantics, plus concrete, artifact‑based recommendations for follow‑on designs that change the estimand to measure repair efficacy under sampling variability.
sections.related_work: Prior literature documents hallucination and reference unreliability as general LLM reliability problems that undermine trust in operational applications [1], and reports that evidence‑grounded generation (RAG) reduces unsupported assertions in operations‑style QA tasks [2]. Tool‑assisted GVR architectures and verifier‑guided feedback loops have shown empirical improvements in infrastructure‑as‑code and program‑generation contexts (for example, TerraFormer and related verifier‑guided approaches), but those demonstrations largely target IaC or program repair rather than device‑level NetOps execution studies [3]. Evaluations of LLM capability for network intent translation exist [4], but standardized execution‑level safety benchmarking in packet‑level simulators and paired estimand semantics remain underexplored in the supplied corpus. These findings motivated a preregistered confirmatory run that preserves strict execution semantics and full artifact accounting so the executed estimand is unambiguous.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered the study (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01). The primary estimand was the per‑intent paired difference in proportion of validator‑valid executable configurations between guarded and baseline (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The preregistration fixed a paired design with task_count = 200, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, primary test = exact McNemar two‑sided, and paired bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000). The preregistration SHA256 is archived with the evidence bundle.

Task bank and contamination checks. A deterministic task generator created a fixed manifest of N = 200 synthetic 'intent_configuration_repair_v1' intents. Each manifest entry records initial_state, required_sequence, difficulty annotation, and generation_seed (representative seeds include 4, 5, 6). The preregistered contamination procedure (SHA256 exact matches and high‑similarity n‑gram checks) ran before execution and flagged no exact‑match exclusions; the analysis/contamination_summary.csv in the archive is empty.

Generation semantics and model configuration. Execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per intent was produced and deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded episodes. Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini via the hosted adapter openai_responses; execution used model_calls_used = 200 (one shared generation per pair). The archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is explicitly reported and is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Provider audit metadata recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and a stage labeled shared_initial_generation = 200 in deterministic reconciliation.

Validator and repair pipeline. Scoring employed deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with scoring_rule = 'full_intent_constraint_validation' that produced a binary valid/invalid executable label. Guarded episodes permitted a single automated repair attempt if the validator flagged violations. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics a repair could only alter the final guarded outcome downstream of the identical initial candidate; baseline reused the same candidate without repair.

Analysis plan. The preregistered primary test is the exact two‑sided McNemar test on the paired 2×2 contingency table; complete_pair_primary excludes incomplete pairs. We report exact p‑values and the paired absolute risk difference with 95% paired bootstrap percentile CIs. Exploratory subgroup and failure‑category tests were declared exploratory and would use Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction if discordant pairs appeared. All analysis artifacts (paired contingency table, condition summaries, missingness table) are archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The adapter executed the preregistered plan: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0; model_calls_used = 200 because one shared initial generation per pair was produced and reused. Deterministic reconciliation confirms complete_pair_count = 200 and consistent episode accounting; provider_call_audit shows cache_miss_count = 200 and cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false, consistent with shared_initial_generation semantics.

Primary outcomes and contingency. Baseline_success_count = 200/200 (100%); guarded_success_count = 200/200 (100%). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) paired percentile 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0]. These numeric results and CSV artifacts are archived under analysis/ with hashes recorded in the execution manifest.

Repair activity and validator traces. Repair_attempt_count = 0 and repair_applied_count = 0 for the entire run because every shared initial candidate passed deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Representative per‑episode scoring JSONs (for example, execution/scoring/task‑000004‑baseline.json, task‑000004‑guarded.json) show identical shared_initial_candidate content, identical normalized_configuration, validator.validation_after.valid = true, and validator.repair_applied = false. The representative tasks include explicit required_sequence entries and difficulty annotations (e.g., 'very_hard' and 'extreme' levels) demonstrating that even tasks labeled as high difficulty produced validator‑valid initial candidates in this sampling regime.

Missingness and contamination. No episodes failed and no items were excluded for contamination; analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 200 and zero failed or unscorable episodes. analysis/contamination_summary.csv contains no flagged items. Deterministic_reconciliation.json demonstrates all deterministic consistency checks passed.

Compact result table. Table 1 (below) provides the paired contingency and repair summary to make the degenerate pathway explicit: all 200 pairs were valid in both arms and zero repair attempts occurred.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The design intentionally isolates the downstream validator/repair effect on an identical sampled candidate. Because the single shared initial candidate per intent was valid under deterministic_netops_validator_v5 for all 200 tasks, the guarded pipeline could not alter any outcome and the paired difference is therefore exactly zero. This is a narrowly scoped, artifact‑grounded scientific conclusion about the executed estimand only; it does not imply GVR architectures are unnecessary more broadly.

Why this degenerate outcome matters scientifically. The run highlights the crucial role of sampling semantics in GVR evaluations: when arms reuse an identical candidate, observed paired differences reflect only post‑generation repairs; if the initial candidate set contains few validator‑detectable faults, guarded repairs have no opportunity to change outcomes. Thus a confirmatory paired null result under shared_initial_candidate semantics communicates a different scientific object than a null result from an independent‑sampling paired design.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics and the single sampled generation per intent constrain inference to validator/repair effects on the same candidate and preclude sampling‑driven differences. Construct validity: the deterministic validator abstractly enforces required constraints and does not execute vendor‑specific CLI or live packet flows; repairs not tested against live device idiosyncrasies. External validity: a single declared model/provider (gpt‑5‑mini via openai_responses), synthetic task bank, and validator abstraction limit generalizability to operational deployments. Conclusion validity: zero discordant pairs produce an uninformative inferential result about repair efficacy under sampling variability; different sampling semantics or adversarial tasks are needed to elicit discordant pairs.

Operational recommendations grounded in artifacts. To evaluate whether GVR pipelines reduce executable misconfiguration rates under realistic variability we recommend preregistered follow‑on designs that (1) produce independent per‑condition first‑pass samples (i.e., remove shared_initial_candidate reuse so each arm receives its own generation), (2) include adversarially crafted or higher‑difficulty task subsets to increase expected discordant counts, (3) explicitly set and record sampling parameters (avoid temperature = null/unset), (4) test multiple model families/providers, and (5) increase validator fidelity (vendor CLI specifics or packet‑level emulation) so repairs can be evaluated against dynamic runtime interactions. Each recommendation changes the estimand and therefore must be preregistered; we provide these as artifact‑grounded, practical next steps.

Reproducibility and representative diagnostics. The evidence bundle archives the preregistration, execution manifest, model configuration, raw responses, per‑episode scoring JSONs, and analysis CSVs. Representative scoring JSON excerpts (e.g., execution/scoring/task‑000004‑baseline.json and task‑000004‑guarded.json) show the same shared_initial_candidate text and validator traces with validator.valid = true and repair_applied = false; these artifact paths and the analysis CSVs support the repair_attempt_count = 0 and repair_applied_count = 0 summary. The execution manifest also records model_calls_used = 200 and completed_episode_count = 400, supporting the provider audit accounting discussed above.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that measured the downstream effect of deterministic validation and one permitted automated repair on a fixed LLM‑generated candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Under these execution semantics (gpt‑5‑mini; model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset) every shared initial candidate passed deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and no repairs were applied; baseline and guarded conditions were therefore identical on the executed estimand (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; bootstrap CI = [0.0,0.0]). This outcome is evidence that, for the sampled candidates and validator used, there were no validator‑detectable faults to repair. Crucially, the preregistered primary estimand was intentionally limited by shared_initial_candidate semantics; an independent per‑condition sampling design constitutes a different estimand and is required to measure repair efficacy when generation sampling variability is present. We contribute a fully artifacted pipeline and precise, artifact‑grounded recommendations for follow‑on preregistered studies that change sampling semantics, increase task difficulty, diversify models, and raise validator fidelity to evaluate GVR impact under realistic operational variability.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure (concise): The human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) before the autonomy lock. After the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature review, experiment selection, preregistration (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01; preregistration_sha256 = f0c8330d3d74cb95461d3f0291ba1b607c427ad37b5edc3750cad593bd4aae76), code generation, execution, deterministic validation, automated analysis, and manuscript drafting without manual human editing of technical content. Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini via hosted adapter 'openai_responses' (execution used model_calls_used = 200; execution/model_configuration.json archived). Generation semantics executed: shared_initial_candidate — exactly one sampled initial generation per intent was produced and deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded conditions (no independent per‑condition first‑pass sampling). The archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 scored candidates; the guarded arm was permitted one automated repair iteration, but in this run the validator flagged no violations and no repairs were applied (repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0). Execution accounting: completed_episode_count = 400 (200 paired intents) with no preregistration deviations. Master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt — SHA256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Pre‑lock infrastructure development and rehearsal occurred but pre‑lock artifacts were not used as empirical evidence in this final run. After the autonomy lock no human manually rewrote technical results, manuscript text, figures, or references.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: a single sampled initial generation was reused across baseline and guarded conditions; this design measures validator/repair effects only and cannot detect differences caused by independent per‑condition sampling or prompt engineering.

Temperature unset (temperature = null) in execution/model_configuration.json: null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; sampling nondeterminism may still have occurred during the single sampled generation.
Single model and single hosted provider: results reflect gpt‑5‑mini under the archived adapter; generalization to other models or model families is unsupported by these artifacts.

Synthetic task bank and validator abstraction: tasks were synthetic 'intent_configuration_repair_v1' items and the deterministic validator is an abstraction; realistic vendor CLI idiosyncrasies, emergent runtime interactions, and hardware effects were not executed on live devices.

No observed validator failures: all initial candidates were validator‑valid, so the experiment could not assess the repair step's effectiveness; the null effect therefore reflects the task bank and sampling semantics rather than evidence that GVR is unnecessary in general.
